kinetics.newton_second_law.title: Newton's second law (F = ma)
assumptions: Net force on a particle (or the mass-centre of a body), in an inertial frame.

kinetics.centripetal_force.title: Centripetal force (F_c = mv²/r = mω²r)
assumptions: Uniform circular motion; the force points toward the centre. Enter either v or ω (with r) — the two are tied by v = ωr.

kinetics.work_constant_force.title: Work done by a constant force (W = F·d·cosθ)
assumptions: Constant force along a straight displacement; W < 0 when the force opposes the motion.

kinetics.potential_energy.title: Gravitational and spring potential energy
assumptions: h measured from an arbitrary datum (PE is relative); x is the spring stretch or compression from its free length.

kinetics.power.title: Mechanical power (P = F·v)
assumptions: Force and velocity in the same direction. Rotational power P = Tω is the shaft-power calculator in the mechanics-of-materials section.

kinetics.efficiency.title: Mechanical efficiency (η = P_out/P_in)
assumptions: Power losses are P_in − P_out = P_in(1 − η).

kinetics.linear_impulse.title: Linear impulse and momentum (J = F·Δt = mΔv)
assumptions: Impulse of a constant average force over Δt equals the change in linear momentum.

kinetics.angular_momentum.title: Angular momentum of a rigid body (H = Iω)
assumptions: About the axis of rotation (a principal axis). For a particle, I = mr² about the axis.

kinetics.restitution.title: Coefficient of restitution (e = (v2′ − v1′)/(v1 − v2))
assumptions: Direct central impact; e = 1 perfectly elastic, e = 0 perfectly plastic. Requires v1 ≠ v2 (bodies approaching).
method_references: Coefficient of restitution e = (v2′ − v1′)/(v1 − v2)

kinetics.impact_velocities.title: Direct central impact: velocities after impact (given e and masses)
assumptions: Direct central impact (motion along the line of centres) with coefficient of restitution e; momentum and the restitution relation are solved together.
method_references: Direct central impact solution from momentum conservation and e = (v2′ − v1′)/(v1 − v2)

kinetics.mass_moment_inertia.title: Mass moment of inertia of a standard solid (plus parallel-axis)

variables.name: d
variables.desc: parallel-axis offset distance (0 for the centroidal axis)

variables.name: I_c
variables.desc: moment of inertia about the centroidal axis
variables.label: Ic

variables.name: I
variables.desc: moment of inertia about the parallel axis (I_c + m·d²)

assumptions: Standard solids about a centroidal principal axis: rod m L²/12; disk/solid cylinder m r²/2; sphere 2mr²/5; thin spherical shell 2mr²/3; block m(a²+b²)/12 (axis ⊥ to the a×b face). Parallel-axis theorem I = I_c + m·d².
method_references: Standard mass moments of inertia; parallel-axis theorem

kinetics.radius_of_gyration.title: Radius of gyration (k = √(I/m))
assumptions: The distance k at which the whole mass could be concentrated to give the same I.

kinetics.rigid_body_planar.title: Rigid-body planar motion: translation and rotation equations

variables.name: M
variables.desc: net moment about the mass centre

variables.name: I_G
variables.desc: mass moment of inertia about the mass centre
variables.label: IG

assumptions: Newton–Euler equations for a rigid body in plane motion: ΣF = m·a_G (translation of the mass centre) and ΣM_G = I_G·α (rotation about the mass centre). For rolling without slipping add a = αr; for a fixed-axis pivot use ΣM_O = I_O·α.
method_references: Plane rigid-body equations of motion: ΣF = m a_G, ΣM_G = I_G α

kinetics.gyroscopic_torque.title: Gyroscopic torque and precession (M = IωΩ)

variables.name: I
variables.desc: spin moment of inertia about the spin axis

assumptions: Spin axis perpendicular to the precession axis; the torque is perpendicular to both. The reaction the spinning body exerts on its supports has the same magnitude.

kinetics.rocket_thrust.title: Rocket thrust (T = ṁ·v_e)
assumptions: Steady propellant mass flow; v_e is the effective exhaust velocity (specific impulse I_sp = v_e/g0). With a nozzle pressure mismatch T = ṁ·v_exit + (p_e − p_a)·A_e, i.e. v_e = v_exit + (p_e − p_a)·A_e/ṁ.

kinetics.tsiolkovsky.title: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation (Δv = v_e·ln(m0/mf))
assumptions: Ideal rocket, no drag or gravity, constant v_e; log is the natural logarithm.

source.derivation: Solid sphere about a diameter: I_c = ⅖mr² = 0.4·5·0.04 = 0.08 kg·m²; with d = 0 the parallel axis adds nothing
Parallel-axis theorem: I = I_c + md² = 0.08 + 5·0.3² = 0.08 + 0.45 = 0.53 kg·m²
a = F/m = 30/5 = 6 m/s²; α = M/I_G = 6/2 = 3 rad/s²
